_doc: Task 65/66 (scripts/systems/street_scenes.gd): the scene library. Every scene comes from a real state: a town drama thread (feud, tension, family rift, affair, debt, addiction or a failing business), two people on a lot who can't stand each other, an elder on the lot, an open case's top suspect (the arrest: a uniformed officer walks in, the real JusticeProcess.arrest), someone with a record or a crew thread at a parked car (the alarm, after dark or on a rough block), the neighbour's real friends round (the party next door, in the evening at home). TownLife plays them where the pawn is (else resolves them off-screen) and the involvement director may pick one. weights = how likely each kind is among those with a cause; stay_min = how long the people stay on the lot; arrest_progress = how far a case must be; party_min = how long the party lasts. Lines use {a} {b} {c} {place}.

row: {a} and {b} are shouting at each other outside {place}.
{a} jabs a finger at {b}. Voices are raised; people are looking.
{a} and {b} are squaring up to each other, outside {place}.
row_fight: {a} shoves {b}. It's turning into a fight outside {place}.
affair: {c} has found {a} and {b} together. "How long has this been going on?"
debt: {b} has {a} backed against the wall. "You know what you owe."
upset: {a} is sitting on their own, crying quietly.
{a} is staring at nothing, eyes red.
collapse: {a} sways, then folds to the ground.
{a} grabs their chest and goes down.
calm_ok: You get between them. "Come on, not here." They back off, still glaring, but it's over.
A few words and they cool down. {a} even nods at you.
calm_fail: "Stay out of it!" {a} rounds on you instead.
Nobody listens. {a} turns on you: "Who asked you?"
watched: You watch it play out. People will be talking about this.
You stay and watch. You won't forget who said what.
walked: Not your business. You move on.
comfort: You sit with {a} for a while. They manage a smile. "Thanks. Really."
comfort_no: {a} wipes their eyes. "I'm fine. Leave it."
debt_ok: "Leave them alone." {b} looks you over, spits, and walks off. For now.
debt_fail: {b} turns to you. "You want some too?" You back off.
ambulance: You call it in and stay with {a} until the ambulance comes.
helped_up: You help {a} sit up. They're shaken. Someone walks them home to rest.
You stay with {a} until they can stand. They go home, grey in the face.
arrest: {b}, a police officer, stops {a}. "You need to come with me." {a} protests, loudly.
A police officer, {b}, takes {a} by the arm. "Down to the station. Now."
vouch: "You've got the wrong person!" The officer notes your name. {a} looks back at you, grateful.
alarm: A car alarm goes off. {a} is bent over a parked car's door.
A car alarm starts wailing. {a} jumps back from a parked car, looking around.
alarm_ok: "Oi! Get away from that!" {a} legs it.
alarm_fail: {a} squares up to you. "Mind your own." You back off.
alarm_police: You call it in. {a} sees you on the phone and walks off fast.
party: Music is thumping through the wall: {a} has people round next door.
Laughter and loud music from {place} next door. {a}'s got friends over.
party_wall: You bang on the wall. The music drops, then creeps back up.
party_bear: You put up with it. It quietens down eventually.
someone_called: Behind you, someone is already on the phone for an ambulance.
